entry.title: Sa Tuna Beach, Begur
entry.summary: Sa Tuna is a tiny cove near Begur on the Costa Brava, with a small beach of coarse sand and a row of whitewashed fishermen houses along the shore. Pine-covered cliffs surround the bay and the water is clear. A coast path links Sa Tuna to the neighbouring coves.

entry.title: Cala Gracio, Ibiza
entry.summary: Cala Gracio is a sheltered cove on the west coast of Ibiza, a short drive north of Sant Antoni de Portmany. The sand is coarse and the water is shallow and clear, with pine-covered hills around the bay. It is quieter than the beaches in town, and sunset views are good.

entry.title: Trpanj Beach, Peljesac
entry.summary: Trpanj is a small fishing village at the northern end of the Peljesac peninsula, with a quiet pebble beach beside the harbour. The water is clear and calm, and ferries cross from here to Ploce on the mainland. The village is far from the main tourist routes.

entry.title: Medena Beach, Seget Vranjica
entry.summary: Medena is a long pebble and shingle beach in Seget Vranjica, a few kilometres west of Trogir in central Dalmatia. Pine trees give shade behind the shore and the water is shallow and clear. The beach is easy to reach and suits families.

entry.title: Praia da Cordoama, Vila do Bispo
entry.summary: Praia da Cordoama is a long, open Atlantic beach near Vila do Bispo in the western Algarve, backed by cliffs and dunes. The waves are strong and attract surfers, and the sand is wide at low tide. It is part of the Costa Vicentina natural park and feels wild.

entry.title: Praia de Afife, Viana do Castelo
entry.summary: Praia de Afife is a wide Atlantic beach with golden sand and dunes on the Minho coast, a short drive north of Viana do Castelo. The waves are good for surf and bodyboarding, and the water is cool even in summer. The beach is quiet outside July and August.

entry.title: Praia da Senhora da Rocha, Porches
entry.summary: Praia da Senhora da Rocha is a golden cove in the central Algarve, with a small white chapel on the headland above the sand. Ochre cliffs frame the beach and the water is clear and sheltered. A set of steps leads down from the car park above.

entry.title: Chiaia di Luna Beach, Ponza
entry.summary: Chiaia di Luna is a long crescent of pebbles on the west coast of Ponza, below a huge curved white cliff. It is reached through an old Roman tunnel from the town. Rockfalls have affected the cliff in the past, so access and swimming rules can change; check local signs before you go.

entry.title: Bergeggi Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Bergeggi is a small village on the Ligurian coast with a pebble beach facing the island of Bergeggi, a protected marine reserve with clear water for snorkelling. A seafront path leads past a medieval tower toward the headland. The place is quieter than the larger Riviera resorts.

entry.title: Varigotti Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Varigotti is a small seaside village on the Ligurian coast with pastel-coloured fishermen houses that face a long beach of fine sand. A cliff path leads to the old quarter and to a small cove called Malpasso. The water is clear and the beach is a favourite with Italian families.

entry.title: Capo Vaticano Beach, Calabria
entry.summary: Capo Vaticano is a headland near Ricadi in Calabria, with granite cliffs, white sand beaches and clear turquoise water. The lighthouse on the cape gives views over the coast and toward the Aeolian Islands on a clear day. This stretch is often called the Coast of the Gods.

entry.title: Sant Andrea Beach, Elba
entry.summary: Sant Andrea is a small sandy cove on the north-west coast of Elba, with smooth granite boulders at both ends. The water is clear and good for snorkelling, and the village above has a few restaurants and hotels. Mount Capanne rises behind the coast.

entry.title: Psarou Beach, Mykonos
entry.summary: Psarou is a sheltered sandy bay on the south coast of Mykonos, and one of the best known beaches on the island. Beach clubs line the sand and the water is clear and calm, protected from the north wind. It is lively and busy in July and August.

entry.title: Myrtos Beach, Ierapetra
entry.summary: Myrtos is a small village on the south coast of Crete with a long beach of grey pebbles and coarse sand in front of whitewashed houses. The water is clear and the setting is quiet, with mountains behind the village. It has a relaxed feel, with tavernas close to the sea.

entry.title: Liapades Beach, Corfu
entry.summary: Liapades is a small village beach on the north-west coast of Corfu, just south of Paleokastritsa. A curve of pebbles and coarse sand sits below green hills, and the water is clear and calm in summer. It is much quieter than Paleokastritsa and has a few tavernas by the shore.

entry.title: Myrtiotissa Beach, Corfu
entry.summary: Myrtiotissa is a long golden beach on the west coast of Corfu, backed by steep green cliffs and a small monastery above. It is reached by a steep path from the road, which keeps it quieter than other beaches on the island. The sea is deep blue and can have waves, and part of the beach is informally used by naturists.

entry.title: Prasonisi Beach, Rhodes
entry.summary: Prasonisi is a sandy spit at the far southern tip of Rhodes, where a narrow sandbar joins the main island to a small rocky islet. The Aegean lies on one side and the Mediterranean on the other, so one side is usually calm and the other is windy. It is a well known spot for windsurfing and kitesurfing in summer.

entry.title: Praia de Galapos, Arrabida
entry.summary: Praia de Galapos is a sheltered bay of pale sand and fine pebbles below the green Arrabida mountains south of Lisbon. The water is clear, calm and turquoise, and the bay is protected by the hills, which makes it one of the nicest swimming beaches near the capital.

entry.title: Praia de Melides, Alentejo
entry.summary: Praia de Melides is a wide, wild beach of pale sand on the Alentejo coast, with a freshwater lagoon behind the dunes and almost no development. The Atlantic is powerful and cool, and the beach feels remote even in summer.

entry.title: Praia dos Salgados, Albufeira
entry.summary: Praia dos Salgados is a long beach of golden sand in the central Algarve, beside a protected coastal lagoon known for its birdlife. The sea is open and often breezy, and the beach is much wider and quieter than the town beaches nearby.

entry.title: Lerici Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Lerici is a colourful harbour town on the Gulf of La Spezia, known as the Gulf of Poets, with a small beach of sand and pebbles below a medieval castle. The water is calm and clear, and narrow streets and pastel houses climb the hill behind.

entry.title: Numana Beach, Marche
entry.summary: Numana is a small town on the Conero Riviera in Marche, with beaches of fine white pebbles and clear green-blue water below the wooded slopes of Monte Conero. The coast is one of the few rocky stretches on the Adriatic, and the beaches here are among the cleanest in Italy.

entry.title: Noli Beach, Liguria
entry.summary: Noli is a small medieval seaside town on the Ligurian Riviera, with a beach of sand and pebbles below the old walls and towers. The water is clear and calm, colourful fishing boats are pulled up on the sand, and the island of Bergeggi sits just offshore.

entry.title: Mazzaro Beach, Taormina
entry.summary: Mazzaro is a pebble bay on the Ionian coast of Sicily, below the hill town of Taormina and connected to it by a cable car. The water is deep blue and clear, and the bay looks out towards the coast and Mount Etna on a clear day.

entry.title: Scivu Beach, Sardinia
entry.summary: Scivu is a wild beach on the Costa Verde of south-west Sardinia, with tall golden dunes that reach down to a long sweep of sand. The sea is open to the Atlantic-style waves of the western coast, and the area has almost no development.

entry.title: Ile-Rousse Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Ile-Rousse is a lively seaside town in the Balagne on the north coast of Corsica, with a long town beach of sand and fine gravel and a small red-rock islet linked to the shore by a causeway. The water is clear and the mountains of the Balagne frame the view.

entry.title: Sagone Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Sagone is a long beach of pale sand at the head of the gulf of the same name on the west coast of Corsica, with a Genoese tower on the point and mountains behind. The water is shallow and the beach is wide, which suits families.

entry.title: Cargese Beach (Peru), Corsica
entry.summary: Peru is a small sandy bay below the village of Cargese on the west coast of Corsica, with clear water and green maquis hills around it. Cargese itself was founded by Greek settlers, and the village has both Catholic and Orthodox churches facing each other.

entry.title: Algajola Beach, Corsica
entry.summary: Algajola is a small walled town in the Balagne on the north-west coast of Corsica, with a Genoese citadel beside a long beach of pale sand. The water is clear and shallow, and the mountains of the interior rise behind the village.

entry.title: Torre del Mar Beach, Velez-Malaga
entry.summary: Torre del Mar is a long beach of dark grey sand on the eastern Costa del Sol, with a wide promenade, palm trees and the mountains of the Axarquia behind. It feels like a Spanish town beach rather than a resort strip.
